DR Congo Seizes Foreign-Owned Gas & Water Utilities Sites Amid Diplomatic Tensions

The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has seized multiple sites operated by foreign-owned Gas & Water Utilities companies in a move that industry observers describe as a significant escalation of ongoing diplomatic tensions. The government’s Ministry of Energy and Hydraulic Resources announced late Tuesday that all assets belonging to foreign entities in the sector, including major treatment plants and distribution centers, are now under state control “pending further notice.”

The measure, which took effect overnight, has impacted at least four large firms, including AquaSource Congo and GazNord RDC, whose local staff reported being escorted from several key sites by security forces. According to the DRC Gas & Water Utilities Workers Union, more than 3,200 employees have been placed on indefinite leave as a result of the seizures. “Our members were informed with no prior warning,” said union representative Jean-Marc Kasongo. “There is widespread uncertainty about jobs and salaries.”

Industry analysts say the move threatens to disrupt sector operations. “This action creates immediate operational challenges, especially regarding maintenance and safe management of sites,” said Louise Mbala, an analyst at Kinshasa-based consultancy Hydrosphere Africa. “The state will have to mobilize experienced personnel quickly to avoid technical setbacks.”

Government officials justified the action as a protective measure, citing “national security concerns,” but did not elaborate further. The Association of Gas & Water Utilities of the Congo issued a statement calling for urgent dialogue, warning that the situation could “jeopardize sector performance if prolonged.”

At the time of writing, the situation remains fluid, with government-appointed administrators reported to be reviewing site operations and personnel files. It is unclear how long the state intends to maintain control or what compensation, if any, will be offered to the affected firms and employees. Stakeholders are closely monitoring developments as the standoff continues.
